Each query inspects at most 256 metadata records, at most 16 per server tick, and detects a 129th permission-filtered candidate before a native observation. RecipientResolver uses required read-only citizen projections with stable citizen/entity/generation/lifecycle identity, visibility/control/permission and current server tick. Namesakes clarify. Unloaded, foreign, private and absent recipients have the same fieldless unavailable result. A bound delivery checks its accepted stable identity and current policy; rename alone cannot reroute it to another citizen who takes the old display name. # Storage metadata format 1 and operator recovery

The format is independent of cc.cd/1.0.0 and A/B journals. Each world has one dedicated metadata directory and one OS file lock. The canonical UTF-8 current file is capped at 8 MiB, uses NFC strings, sorted keys, integer-only numbers and exactly one LF. Every record requires its complete frozen StorageRecord fields, including explicit ACL; each assignment requires complete StorageRoleAssignment fields. No quantity, reservation, Job, credit or effect state is admitted.

The outer object has exactly `checksum_sha256` and `payload`. The checksum is SHA-256 of the canonical payload bytes including their final LF. The payload has exactly `schema` (`cc.storage-metadata/1`), `world_id`, `revision`, `records`, `assignments` and `bindings`. Records are sorted by storage UUID; assignments by beneficiary kind/UUID/role; binding references by storage UUID. Duplicate storage IDs or beneficiary-role keys fail closed. Storage/assignment worlds must match the directory's expected server world. Assignment generations may remain stale after a tombstone, but stale references never resolve.

| File | Meaning |
|---|---|
| metadata.current.json | Current checksummed snapshot; only this metadata acknowledgement advances the caller's revision. |
| metadata.previous.json | Last valid current snapshot, staged/forced before replacing current. |
| metadata.pending.json | Uncommitted candidate, forced before replacement; ordinary open never promotes it. |
| metadata.previous.pending.json | Staged previous copy. An interrupted copy preserves all originals and requires operator reconciliation. |
| metadata.lock | OS ownership lock; a second owner opens read-only. |

A write checks current-file fingerprint and free replacement/rollback headroom, creates/forces pending, creates/forces the previous copy, atomically replaces previous, atomically replaces current, forces the directory, then acknowledges. Unsupported atomic move or force operations cause read-only failure rather than a weaker durability path. Queue overflow returns BUSY without caller-thread IO. Disk headroom failure returns STORAGE_FULL before touching snapshot files and can be retried after space returns. No identity or tombstone is evicted to make room.

An error makes the live owner read-only without claiming the candidate acknowledged. After a process kill, ordinary open accepts a fully valid current/previous lineage or remains read-only with all original files. A valid replacement may be visible even if the old caller never received acknowledgement; retry with an old expected revision conflicts. This is metadata atomicity, never item transfer, participant-save durability or original-owner settlement.

## Migration and coordinated rollback rules

1. Stop the metadata owner and use the qualified A/world maintenance lifecycle before changing files. Preserve byte-for-byte copies of the entire metadata directory, associated native world and actual A save lineage. Never edit live files under an active owner.
2. Inspect versions, checksums, world IDs, revisions, pending/previous files and the recorded native/A lineage. The normal opener never repairs, deletes, promotes pending, rewrites unknown formats or widens ACLs. A valid previous file is only a read-only diagnostic view when current is missing/corrupt/unsupported.
3. An unsupported version needs a separately versioned, reviewed migration with old/new fixtures, explicit owner/ACL policy and verified rollback compatibility. Missing ACL or owner fields remain untrusted; they must not become public/default grants. Preserve original unknown bytes while producing a separate reviewed candidate.
4. Coordinate any rollback with the actual native world and A participant-save history. Metadata-only rollback cannot establish identity continuity against a newer native marker/world. Generation counters are not proof against rolling both histories back. D02 must reobserve binding incarnations/topology after restart or rollback; J/A must qualify effects and custody.
5. Reopen a reviewed compatible current/previous set under the expected world, then explicitly revalidate native bindings and authorization before integration. Keep uncertain records unverified and preserve the archived originals. D01 offers no automatic recovery/promotion command and no inventory compensation.

J01 owns the real metadata directory/retention lifecycle adapter. D01 tests exercise temporary metadata files and real terminated JVMs only; they do not execute a Minecraft world or establish native save evidence.

# D01 metadata API

Package: `dev.aivillages.core.kernel.storage`. No Minecraft/Fabric imports, native initializer, scheduler, inventory/effect/Job ledger or retention owner is added.

| Type/API | Contract |
|---|---|
| StorageRegistryLimits | Hard ceilings of 4096 records including tombstones, 4096 beneficiary-role keys, 32 grants/record, four purpose roles and an 8 MiB current snapshot. Custom limits can only tighten them. The write reserves three snapshot sizes plus 64 KiB of free replacement/rollback headroom. |
| StorageRegistry.Snapshot | Immutable world/revision, UUID-keyed records, separate beneficiary-role assignments and strict binding references. Binding metadata is never live native authority. |
| StorageRegistry.Record | World+storage UUID identity, NFC display label, owner, purpose roles, explicit ACL, revision/generation/ACL revision, state and finite adapter ID. Registration is PENDING_BIND. |
| StorageRegistry.Authority | Explicit pure server-adapter policy for caller/subject control and record operations. No permissive production default. It runs on the IO owner and must not call native game-thread objects. |
| registerMetadata | CAS on world revision, owner control and registration authority; returns a new stable UUID only after metadata acknowledgement. |
| rename / updateAcl / tombstone | CAS on world and record revisions plus operation-specific policy. Rename preserves identity/generation; ACL replacement requires grant and revoke authority; tombstone increments generation and retains the identity. |
| assignRole | Separate `(world, beneficiary, role)` map. Expected assignment revision -1 creates; a matching nonnegative revision explicitly reassigns. PUBLIC is not a beneficiary. Storage generation is checked at lookup; stale/tombstoned references do not resolve. |
| queryVisible / roleMetadata | Pure permitted metadata views. Lookup folds names without granting authority or choosing the first namesake. Neither method resolves physical inventory or grants access. |
| StorageMetadataStore.open | Returns a future; filesystem operations run on the bounded dedicated IO worker. Missing/corrupt/unsupported originals are preserved read-only, with a compatible previous snapshot used only as a diagnostic view. |
| StorageMetadataStore.createNew | Explicit future-based initialization of a new directory only. It never overwrites an existing directory or imports a legacy record permissively. |
| closeAsync | Returns immediately; queued mutations finish before lock/file closure on the IO worker. No caller-thread filesystem close or unbounded fallback queue. |
| Ack | ACKNOWLEDGED, REVISION_CONFLICT, DENIED, READ_ONLY, LIMIT, STORAGE_FULL, BUSY, INVALID or IO_ERROR, with revision and optional storage UUID. Successful reason is METADATA_ONLY_ACK; it is not an A receipt or Minecraft save proof. |
| StorageMetadataCodec | Strict canonical UTF-8 metadata schema/checksum and frozen cc.cd validation for records/assignments/binding references. Unknown fields, inventory/Job/credit data, missing ACLs and duplicate identities fail closed. |

NFC labels keep their display spelling. Lookup uses the pinned Unicode 16.0 default full case-fold C/F data, including expansions and non-ASCII special cases. The generated table and official source/license/provenance live in the D-owned source prefix; no new runtime dependency or version migration is introduced. Java 25's Unicode baseline is unchanged. The source digest is `6f1f9c588eb4a5c718d9e8f93b782685e5c7fec872cf05e8e6878053599e09bb`.

Records describe purpose roles; assignments describe beneficiary defaults. A shared or organization-owned chest can be a citizen's default while its owner and ACL remain unchanged. Names and metadata bytes never grant native access. D02 must establish/revalidate native bindings, D04 supplies access semantics, and J01/J02 supply actual authenticated ingress/lifecycle/A authority. The module remains inert until integration.

# D02 API and native hook boundary

`StorageBindingRules` in core has immutable Member, Topology and Binding values. It canonicalizes members by (x,y,z,incarnation UUID), rejects unsupported shapes, duplicate members, nonadjacent/vertical double chests and incorrect facing axes, and hashes the frozen canonical topology JSON including its final LF. Wire encoding/decoding passes through D's unchanged cc.cd/1.0.0 codec. Endpoint identity also includes a live lifecycle epoch. These values carry no authorization or save tier.

`StorageRegistry.prepareBinding` checks caller/world, optimistic global and record revisions, fresh supplied BIND policy and the next binding generation. It writes UNKNOWN intent through the same bounded metadata owner before native writes. First binding remains PENDING_BIND; rebinding advances generation/revision and becomes UNVERIFIED. `acknowledgeBinding` requires that exact intent, an actual matching live observation and supplied COMMIT_BIND policy, rechecked before IO. It records ACTIVE metadata after acknowledgement. The authority provider must attest native observations; wire input is never its authority. Loss or denial between steps leaves a non-live pending history. This is not an inventory/effect journal or cross-owner save settlement.

`StorageIncarnationAdapter` requires a ServerLevel, stable world UUID and explicit supplied policy; construction/install and every native operation require the server thread. One owner is allowed per level. `updateMetadata` installs an acknowledged immutable snapshot and builds bounded position/marker indexes outside any scheduled tick. `plan` captures exact loaded block-entity instances and lifecycle versions, creates prospective UUIDs only on the server, and writes no markers. `write` requires the durable exact intent and unchanged instances/topology/lifecycle, rechecks provided native authority, uses a private one-use marker permit, then returns a live observation. No catch-all Container support exists.

# D00 implemented API

Package: `dev.aivillages.core.kernel.storage.contract`. The domain layer imports no Minecraft, Fabric or Fabric-adapter classes. No entrypoint, scheduler, registry writer, Job/effect writer or world-authority factory is added to production.

| API | Observable contract |
|---|---|
| `StorageCodec.decode(String)` / `decode(byte[])` | Validate canonical UTF-8 cc.cd/1.0.0 envelope, exact schema, then frozen cross-field semantics. Return an immutable `StorageWire.Message`, or `StorageCodec.Invalid` with INVALID_SCHEMA/INVALID_SEMANTICS. Bytes must include exactly the canonical final LF. |
| `StorageCodec.encode(Message)` | Deterministic sorted-key compact JSON with one LF. Explicit null fields are preserved. |
| `StorageCodec.evaluate(Message, StorageWire.Context)` | Compare the projection with separate in-process observations and return VALID or REFUSED_EXPECTED. This performs no world observation, admission, resume, transfer or settlement. |
| `StorageWire.Message.kind()` / `body()` | Read-only kind and deeply immutable body, including nested maps/lists. A public message constructor is not exposed. |
| `StorageWire.Context` | Nullable contextual observations: trusted generation, requirement satisfaction, authenticated/question principals, current incarnation, current ACL revision, authenticated A-proof flag and eligible registered count. Never read this record from chat/wire input or treat it as a world-authority capability. |

The 17 envelope kinds are DialogueIntent, PlayerReplyIntent, AssistanceRequest, BlockerEvidence, StorageSelector, StorageRecord, PhysicalStorageBinding, StorageAccessDecision, ResolvedEndpoint, MobilityGoal, DeliveryGoal, CustodyCheckpoint, ActivityResumeSignal, VersionRevisionGeneration, SelectionWitness, StorageRoleAssignment and StageManifest. Their exact fields, variants, ranges and cross-field rules remain in the unchanged [field dictionary](contracts/FIELD_DICTIONARY.md), [schema](contracts/contract.schema.json), [ports](contracts/PORTS.md) and [semantic rules](contracts/semantic-rules.json).

Transport decoding is bounded to 65,536 UTF-8 bytes, depth 48 and 16,384 value/key tokens. Floating numbers, unsafe integers, duplicate keys, non-NFC strings, malformed UTF-8/surrogates, BOM, unknown fields/versions and noncanonical wire bytes are refused. Per-field limits are further restricted by the frozen schema. The embedded schema is checked against SHA-256 `99901b31634957fa8d1c3ebeaa668a5ab4297139a98a015bde81f7e5b89c6589` at class initialization.

VALID means the projection satisfies its structural/semantic/contextual checks. It grants no permission or physical truth. In particular, a decoded ALLOW or A-proof reference is not native authority. Only the deferred J adapter may supply actual authenticated ingress, effect-time observations and qualified A APIs. Context absence in a synthetic fixture is not authorization for a player action.

D00 does not implement metadata persistence, storage resolution, native binding, transfers, movement or conversational runtime behavior. D01 next implements registry metadata and bounded persistence within the same ownership boundary. J01/J02 install production registration/authority adapters later.

# D03 policy API and privacy boundary

`StorageAccessPolicy` is pure Java under `core/kernel/storage`. It requires an immutable snapshot supplier, OrganizationMembershipPort, ControlPort, ProtectionPort and a current server tick supplier. No permissive constructor/default port or public Decision constructor exists. Scope consists of authenticated world/domain/principal plus optional controlled citizen actor; constructing or decoding a wire DTO never supplies those ports or native authority.

`evaluate(scope, storage, operation)` independently checks INSPECT, DEPOSIT, WITHDRAW, ASSIGN, RENAME, GRANT and REVOKE. Runtime operations require ACTIVE registered metadata, its acknowledged binding reference, an explicit matching ACL operation and a current matching native projection. PLAYER grants match principal; CITIZEN grants match the exact actor and fresh control projection; ORGANIZATION grants require current known member rights; PUBLIC grants contain only explicitly configured inspect/deposit/withdraw. A metadata owner does not implicitly receive operation permissions. Organization-owned records additionally obey the current organization policy, so unknown organization state denies access. Known outsider permissions can only come from an explicit trusted organization policy plus an explicit record grant.

`OrganizationMembershipPort.observe(scope, organizations)` is a single read-only IO-free batch of at most 33 organization IDs. Its scope and monotonic membership revision fence decisions; no organization display name is consulted. Missing membership is UNKNOWN. ControlPort returns scope/subject/revision/known/control/delegation facts. ProtectionPort returns exact scope/storage/operation/generation/tick and native policy revision. Stale, mismatched, missing or UNKNOWN native facts cannot allow; the native provider may veto every mod allow. J01 must supply those current projections from qualified existing owners, without importing their implementation into D.

`Decision.current` re-evaluates policy even inside its two-tick validity window and compares scope/actor, operation, world/domain/principal, global registry revision, record revision, binding generation, ACL revision, owner and dependency revisions. Restoring rights at a later revision does not revive an old decision. `authorizesEffect` additionally requires ALLOW. These methods observe a point in time; J02 must call them in the same non-yielding authorized server critical section as an actual effect. They are not leases or A capabilities.

`Decision.wire` projects the unchanged cc.cd/1.0.0 StorageAccessDecision for server-side seams. A decoded ALLOW cannot construct the opaque in-process decision. Refusal projections may contain server-side requested identity/revisions and must not be sent directly to clients. StorageVisibility is the presentation boundary.

`StorageVisibility.lookup` returns either Visible(storage UUID, label, adapter, generation) or the same fieldless Unavailable singleton for missing/private/unknown/stale targets. `enumerate` and `named` return immutable visible entries only, sorted by stable identity. Matching uses the D01 Unicode/NFC casefold and never adds hidden matches or totals. No stock, ACL, owner data, filtered counts or private reason is exposed. Deposit-only callers can select an explicitly shared endpoint without gaining an INSPECT decision. Snapshot changes during discovery refuse publication of mixed results. This is a finite 4096-record scan, not a persistent discovery index or scheduled task.

`mayAdminister` separately checks current owner control and native administrative veto/delegation ceiling. PLAYER administration requires actual matching principal plus control; CITIZEN administration uses current citizen control; ORGANIZATION administration uses current trusted administrator/member policy; PUBLIC administration requires explicitly supplied operator control. This separate path permits administration of an empty private ACL without granting automation access. It does not install itself as StorageRegistry.Authority.

StorageRegistry adds `grant`, `revoke` and `transferOwnership`, preserving expected global/record revisions and its sole bounded asynchronous metadata IO owner. Authority.mayGrant and mayTransfer default to false. Initial ACL seeding, bulk replacement and individual grant require explicit delegation policy; current owner/control/action/ceiling is rechecked immediately before the pending write. Grant cannot widen beyond the provided operations. Revoke cannot imply grant. Duplicate ACL subjects are rejected rather than merged on load. A future malformed/ambiguous legacy snapshot remains read-only; no migration silently invents rights.

Transfer clears ACL and bindings, increments record/ACL/identity generations, sets UNVERIFIED, and retains older role references as stale. It never changes physical inventory or inherits the old owner's grant. A new owner needs a fresh explicit policy and binding. Registration/transfer target consent and native protection are J01 responsibilities behind the required supplied authority; text claiming ownership is never accepted by D. The metadata IO worker must read immutable current revocation projections, not call a game-thread native API. Existing registered data with unique ACL subjects retains the cc.storage-metadata/1 shape.

Test-only StorageAclSequenceProbe and StoragePolicyTestSupport supply synthetic projections in core test output and are explicitly prohibited from the release JAR. The probe creates actual metadata files and executes 100 transitions without resetting its history. The Python oracle independently checks canonical checksums, UUID/scope/operation/tick fences, every revision/generation/owner/ACL transition, old-decision refusal, fresh controls and final persisted state. Those observations have no native/client/root/save tier. The prior D02 standalone fixture is repeated unchanged as a physical regression and remains absent from production descriptors.

## Resulting behavior

The D-owned pure Java registry stores metadata only. Registration produces PENDING_BIND until the future native binding adapter validates a target. Renames preserve world/storage UUID and generation. NFC display labels retain their spelling; pinned Unicode 16 full case folding affects lookup only. Namesakes remain ambiguous. Snapshot/record/assignment expected revisions prevent lost writes: two concurrent writes at one revision acknowledge exactly one.

Beneficiary defaults are a separate `(world, beneficiary, role)` table. Duplicate creation conflicts; reassignment requires the exact existing revision and explicit beneficiary/target authority. Shared or organization-owned storage can be a citizen's default without transferring ownership or adding ACL grants. Purpose roles do not act as defaults. Tombstones retain identities, advance generation and invalidate stale assignments, including after restart. Administrative policy is rechecked immediately before a write.

One bounded dedicated IO worker owns immutable snapshots and the world-directory file lock. It reserves replacement/rollback headroom, writes and forces a pending snapshot, stages and forces the previous copy, atomically replaces current, forces the directory, then acknowledges metadata. Queue overflow refuses without caller-thread IO. Missing, corrupt, unsupported, foreign-world, stale-pending and externally changed files preserve originals and open/read-fail safely. Only explicit fresh-directory initialization can create a new store. Disk-full refusal occurs before changing snapshot files; it does not evict identities or tombstones.

Hard limits are 4096 records/world including tombstones, 4096 beneficiary-role assignments, 32 ACL grants/record, four purpose roles and an 8 MiB serialized current snapshot. Versions, checksums, canonical bytes, complete ACLs, key uniqueness, worlds and referenced generations are strict. Inventory counts, Jobs, reservations, credits and effects are not part of the format. A metadata acknowledgement is not a Minecraft save acknowledgement.

# D04 resolution API and trusted observation boundary

StorageResolver and StorageResolution live in core/kernel/storage; RecipientResolver lives in core/kernel/logistics. All are inert pure Java. Constructors require every port and an authenticated server tick supplier. No Minecraft/Fabric dependency, automatic production registration, IO worker, tick task, discovery index, movement or inventory mutation is added.

`StorageResolver.begin(scope, StorageSelector, operation)` accepts only a strict decoded frozen StorageSelector and INSPECT/DEPOSIT/WITHDRAW. The selector is untrusted data. `Query.step()` advances at most 16 metadata records once per increasing server tick; a second call during the same tick returns the same state. PENDING has no endpoint. Truncation at 256 inspected records or discovery of a 129th permission-filtered candidate returns UNKNOWN. Full scans choose only eligible observed candidates, with exact named ambiguity checked across visible matches. A missing citizen default returns CLARIFY even if an arbitrary nearby chest exists. Type filtering supports only chest single/double and barrel.

`NativePort.view(scope,tick)` must return a fresh authenticated View with lifecycle epoch, monotonic complete query revision and server caller/controlled-actor positions. Its revision must cover all registered-candidate load/topology/capacity/protection, caller visibility, organization membership and citizen control changes that could alter the answer, including previously denied candidates. If this complete observation cannot be supplied, complete must be false and the query returns UNKNOWN. J01 is responsible for the actual projection from existing owners. Query methods must run on the server actor; no port may force chunk loads or execute inventory effects. Anchor positions are captured only from this port, never decoded player coordinates. Later position movement does not rerank the captured query.

`NativePort.observe` must return exact scope/binding/generation/lifecycle/tick, supported/loaded flags and operation-specific capacity eligibility from the native adapter. Every binding member is within radius 16 horizontal and +/-4 vertical relative to the captured anchor. Canonical first-member block-center squared milliblock distance orders candidates, followed by x/y/z and canonical UUID. Distance bounds are tested before multiplication. UNKNOWN/ineligible capacity, unsupported or unloaded native state cannot win. Stored acknowledged binding identity must match the fresh native topology/incarnation/generation and epoch. The final winner is observed and authorized again; a changed final answer returns UNKNOWN without reranking a fallback.

`SelectionPort.consume` retrieves and consumes only an actual server-retained selection for authenticated scope/selection UUID. Its returned Selection contains a strict frozen SelectionWitness plus the registered storage identity. The resolver checks the exact requested selection ID, scope/world/domain/principal, dimension/lifecycle, capture/expiry, registered member coordinates/type and fresh native binding. `SelectionPort.current` must independently verify that retained caller/actor identity, current reach/line-of-sight/protection and native block-entity live-instance token still match the actual server object/topology. Decoding or constructing witness data does not install this port or create a retained capability. Unregistered selected chests cannot be discovered or marked by D04. Witnesses expire within the frozen maximum 40 ticks and do not survive restart.

StorageResolution has fieldless PENDING/CLARIFY/UNAVAILABLE/UNKNOWN/UNSUPPORTED dispositions, or a server-created opaque Bound endpoint. Refusal results carry no private UUID, label, count, stock, ACL or hidden reason. `Query.work()` is a server-only diagnostic (inspected records, candidate counter and tick), never a client projection. The overflow counter may report 129 only to prove the refusal; no 129th native candidate is observed or ranked.

`Bound.current(scope)` re-observes complete view, snapshot, accepted citizen control (for roles), D03 Decision and native identity/capacity/selection. It rechecks the view/snapshot after observations. The accepted decision expires after two ticks and must be resolved again; a wire ALLOW cannot mint a Bound. `Bound.wire()` supplies the strict frozen STORAGE ResolvedEndpoint only while current. It remains a projection. J02 must use the same current observations and effect critical section; the endpoint is not an A capability, lease, save witness or settlement.

`RecipientResolver.Port.view` is an immutable complete bounded list (maximum 256), scoped to the authenticated caller and current tick. Its monotonic revision covers name, visibility/control/load/identity/policy changes; epoch fences restart. `lookup` returns a fresh immutable Citizen projection for the exact requested stable citizen ID. A Citizen includes scope, epoch, citizen/entity UUID, generation/policy revision, display name, dimension, inventory revision digest, tick, visible/controlled/loaded and explicit permitted operations. These are server observations, never accepted from client endpoint claims. A role beneficiary requires current control; a visible permitted recipient can remain usable without granting caller control or inventory inspection. The query scans at most 16 rows per tick and 128 visible eligible citizens; direct addressed/explicit-ID lookup still enforces scope/epoch/visibility/control/permission/load. Missing/private/unloaded/foreign gives uniform UNAVAILABLE. Display labels match by the same frozen NFC/Unicode fold, with no fuzzy selection.

A recipient Bound privately retains the accepted citizen/entity/generation/epoch/policy identity. `fresh(scope)` looks up that stable ID, revalidates all live permissions/control/load and returns an immutable current projection; it never searches the old name. Renames alone preserve the bound recipient, while entity replacement, generation change, policy revocation, unload or caller swap fail closed. J04 projects this current identity into the frozen CITIZEN seam before requesting A/B work. No new citizen registry, POI registry or second persistence owner is introduced.

Test-only StorageResolutionTestSupport and StorageResolutionProbe are explicitly rejected from production packaging. Probe data and timings are pure port observations with null integrated roots/save proof. Existing D02 physical fixtures are unchanged and repeated separately; their native evidence does not upgrade D04's synthetic projections to production/client proof.

# D02 — Physical storage incarnation and chest topology

Status: **OWNED_GATES_PASS**. [Actions run 40672315339, attempt 1](https://github.com/senavirathne/CognitiveCraft-public/actions/runs/40672315339) completed successfully on the first candidate. Independent readiness remains deferred to D11; production integration remains deferred to J.

Predecessor is qualified D01: source `ea1ff7ec9ab1fd16782c32130207aa7e5230442a`, tree `4890dae733de13eb74fa1c9827e50215d4fa2cce`, production JAR SHA-256 `8aaea7d9a69874c1a975d31acade6110c3f9bfa7b35e46125eaa4c699f772cc0`, final docs `3fd622e0d7b4c24762da3b6cd12ab85b6380db83`, run 40662229204 attempt 1. Its 90 owned Java and 42 Python cases passed, with zero native/client credit. Source/docs retain their frozen B ancestry; no A/C implementation is imported.

The design input remains documentation commit `37fbf49e2aec4eddb3c7600217e585a1b349e48f`, D02. The frozen cc.cd/1.0.0 contract manifest/schema and all 57 fixtures remain byte-identical.

D02 implements pure topology values, a metadata-owner UNKNOWN intent followed by explicit native marker writes and acknowledged binding publication, and an inert native adapter for normal chest, complementary double chest and barrel. Coordinate equality, a label or a marker grants no access. Replacement uses a new incarnation; topology rebind advances metadata generation, leaving older role references stale. Duplicate markers quarantine conflicting endpoints. See [D02_API.md](D02_API.md).

The standalone D fixture is the only descriptor that loads the new marker mixin. Existing production descriptors, Jobs/A custody, global entrypoints and peer paths remain protected. J01 owns production installation/retention and caller policy, J02 owns fresh access/effect integration, and J05 owns cross-owner torn-save settlement. A witnessed marker reload is not A participant-save proof.

The frozen candidate schedule repeats all prior owned tests and all three module suites, adding 10 Java tests (100 cumulative), 8 Python tests (50 cumulative), and four owned native cases. Native cases are D02-GT01 replacement/rename, D02-GT02 topology/clone, D02-GT02 composite cold reload, and D02-PERF lifecycle cost. The reload case requires two separate JVMs sharing one isolated saved world; five owned XML observations represent four cases. A sixth JVM measures the exact unchanged D01 JAR and is supporting performance evidence, not a new D02 pass. Vanilla always-pass XML records never inflate owned counts. Connected clients remain zero.

Case identities, seed 20261027, deadlines, 1100 MiB JVM heap, 8192-marker observation/quarantine/retirement limits and performance bounds are frozen in the D-owned case registry before the first candidate Actions request. The same 200 warmup plus 2000 native barrel state changes run against D01 without D hooks and against the candidate with an active binding. Candidate p99 must be at most max(2 ms, 10 × baseline p99), max at most 250 ms, heap below 1100 MiB; existing thresholds remain unchanged. There is no scheduled D per-tick work or chunk-loading/retention owner. Metadata remains bounded by D01 limits and uses its existing asynchronous IO worker.

Raw collection records actual native XML, snapshot sequences, runtime/JAR/fixture hashes, six process exits, selected fixture bytes, bytecode discovery, persisted metadata and compressed native chunk bytes with hashes. The independent oracle decodes the saved NBT, recomputes topology digests, requires native marker/state evidence and refuses missing/duplicate observations, principal swaps, changed binaries, invented percentile values or fabricated integrated settlement. No JSON pass flag alone establishes success.

Local diagnostics exercised the pinned SDK but are not qualified source/JAR evidence. The user authorized Actions and Docker to resolve local dependencies and blocking tests; the existing single D workflow performs one candidate production build, restores the digest-locked D01 baseline artifact, and runs the required native schedule inside the established D-isolated Docker environment.
